pick.headline: Bush and Yeltsin sign START II
pick.summary: On January 3, 1993, Presidents George Bush and Boris Yeltsin signed the START II treaty in Moscow, agreeing to cut strategic nuclear warheads by about two-thirds and eliminate land-based multiple-warhead missiles.
pick.significance: It was the deepest arms-reduction agreement yet negotiated, signed weeks before Bush left office. Its ratification became entangled in Russian domestic politics.
pick.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of January 4, 1993, carried a Budapest Kossuth Radio interview with a Hungarian official who called the signing of START II "so important", saying it would stabilize Yeltsin's position and that ratification depended on how far the United States helped Russia.

alternates.headline: Noriega surrenders to US forces
alternates.summary: On January 3, 1990, Panamanian strongman Manuel Noriega, who had taken refuge in the Vatican nunciature after the US invasion, surrendered to American troops and was flown to Miami to face drug charges.
alternates.significance: Noriega had for years been a paid US intelligence asset before becoming an indictment target. His capture ended Operation Just Cause and raised enduring questions about Washington's dealings with him.
